text:
ravi: FYI discovered a PII leak in the CLI sample (sdk-dotnet) when exercising token refresh in the background worker. The first log line prints the user email; the retry path later prints [REDACTED]. Looks like the redact hook isn't active for the very first log emitted during the refresh.

ravi: repro: (linux)
```
dotnet run --project examples/cli --watch=false
# in another terminal: curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/force-expire
# CLI triggers background refresh and makes request
```

ravi: logs extracted from run:
```
2026-07-14T09:12:01.011Z ERROR background-worker Request failed for user: pete@example.org attempt=1 traceid=00-aaa-111-01
2026-07-14T09:12:01.220Z INFO background-worker Retrying attempt=2 traceid=00-bbb-222-01
2026-07-14T09:12:01.421Z ERROR background-worker Request failed for user: [REDACTED] attempt=2 traceid=00-bbb-222-01
```

zoe: interesting. Two suspects: 1) redact hook initializes async (rules fetch) and misses early logs, 2) retry code is creating a new trace/span for attempt 2 which is why traceid changes. The redact hook uses otel context to decide what to redact; if the span flips, timing matters.

marta: on dotnet there's also a known init ordering quirk: logging providers are registered in Program.cs and some middleware do late patching. If the redact middleware is registered after the logging provider, we see raw logs until the next sync point.

ravi: current init call in sample: `Telemetry.Init(options => { options.Hooks.Add(OtelHook); options.Hooks.Add(RedactHook); options.Hooks.Add(LogBridge); });` we assumed list order is execution order. seems not guaranteed for our host builder.

zoe: quick interim fixes we could land in examples: 1) add a tiny baked-in rule set (email, sk- tokens) that the redact hook applies synchronously during startup so no window leaks, 2) ensure the retry middleware sets a stable attempt header `x-rw-attempt` and reuses it across attempts, 3) patch logging provider earlier in Program.cs to guarantee hook ordering.

marta: for the SDK change: change retry code in sdk-dotnet to compute `attemptId = request.Headers.TryGetValues("x-rw-attempt", out v) ? v : Guid.NewGuid().ToString(); request.Headers.Remove("x-rw-attempt"); request.Headers.Add("x-rw-attempt", attemptId);` then preserve it for the duration of that logical request. That avoids spinning a new id per attempt.

tony: small nuance: some customers rely on the traceid flipping to signal a new logical span per retry (they use it for observability). We should make the attempt-id invariant but leave trace/span behavior configurable: `TelemetryOptions.RetryCreatesNewSpan = true|false` so teams can opt-in.

zoe: agree. Also add an opt-in boolean `redactOnAllLogLevels` for sampleapps so debug/trace also get redacted during dev runs; SDK default stays conservative to avoid perf cost in production.

telemetry-bot: Please open a GH issue and label `devex, telemetry, security`. Attach the captured logs and mark severity: high for sample apps (PII exposure).

ravi: will open GH issue + PR in examples/cli: baked-in fallback rules + Program.cs reorder + unit test. Also a small patch proposal for sdk-dotnet to preserve `x-rw-attempt` and add the `RetryCreatesNewSpan` flag. Tests: add unit test capturing Console output and asserting no email regex present after running expired-token flow.

marta: test note: dotnet logging can buffer; in unit tests wrap Console.SetOut with a StringWriter to capture logs consistently. Use `Regex.IsMatch(output, "[a-z0-9._%+-]+@[a-z0-9.-]+\\.[a-z]{2,}")` to fail if any email present.

tonY: tiny pedant: ensure header casing uses canonical `x-rw-attempt` lower-case since some proxies lower-case headers. Document header semantics in SDK retry spec.

ravi: repro env: dotnet 8.0, sdk-dotnet 0.8.0, opentelemetry-dotnet 1.9.0. Opening issue/PR in ~45m. :thumbsup:
